messages.author: d24e3e0d2299ccfd
messages.subject: Inverse-Wishart Prior
parts:
I am trying to implement an inverse-Wishart prior for tau in the eight schools example. It's not a multivariate tau, but I just wanted to try the 1x1 case, so that I could match the results using MCMCglmm, which uses an inverse-Wishart prior.

I can get my code to run, but somehow it's not producing any results:

model.code <- "
  data {
    int<lower=0> J; // number of schools
    real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
    real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
  } 
  transformed data {
    cov_matrix[1] S;
    S[1, 1] <- 0.001;
  }
  parameters {
    real mu; 
    cov_matrix[1] tau;
    real eta[J];
  }
  transformed parameters {
    vector[J] theta;
    for (i in 1:J) 
      theta[i] <- mu + to_vector(tau)[1]*eta[i];
  }
  model {
    tau ~ inv_wishart(0.001, S);
    eta ~ normal(0, 1);
    y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
  }"

The trouble with the inv_wishart function is that it returns a matrix. I had to figure out how to cast that 1x1 matrix into a real. The best I could do is to_vector(tau)[1], since there is no to_real.

Can someone help me figure out the best to implement the inv-Wishart prior?

Shyue-Ming

parts:
I just ended up using the inv_gamma function, as a univariate special case of inv_wishart.

So the code becomes:

model.code <- "
  data {
    int<lower=0> J; // number of schools 
    real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
    real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates 
  }

parameters {
    real mu; 
    real<lower=0> tau;

real theta[J];
    for (j in 1:J)
      theta[j] <- mu + tau * eta[j];
  }
  model {
    eta ~ normal(0, 1);
    tau ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001);
    y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
  }"

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Inverse-Wishart Prior
parts:
You can read a paper by Andrew on why the inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001)
is especially bad for situations like the 8 schools. It's the
case study for why this is a bad prior. See either the Bayesian
Data Analysis book or the papers referenced in the recommended prior
sections of the regression chapter of the manual.

We also don't recommend (inverse) Wishart; there you want to follow
the link to the Ben Goodrich paper on visualizing multivariates to
understand why.

- Bob
